turns.text:
As a professor, I must say I've never heard of such a curriculum change! However, it does bring up an interesting point about cognitive flexibility and creative thinking. If students were forced to think outside the box and provide unexpected answers, they might develop more innovative ways of problem-solving.

In psychology, this is often associated with divergent thinking – the ability to come up with many unique, novel solutions to a problem. While this new approach might be challenging, it could potentially foster creativity and originality in students. But remember, it's crucial to also learn and understand the conventional answers as well. Let's discuss some interesting psychological theories related to creative thinking during our next session!
